subject: Cloud Computing
title: GitOps: Infrastructure as Code 2.0
description: One-minute skill: GitOps: Infrastructure as Code 2.0.

hook.text: What if your Git repository was the single source of truth for all infrastructure? Commit to deploy. Revert to rollback.

buildup.text: GitOps treats infrastructure definitions like application code: versioned, reviewed, and automatically reconciled.

discovery.text: Tools like ArgoCD and Flux continuously sync your cluster state with your Git repo. Drift is detected and corrected.

twist.text: GitOps makes audit trails automatic. Every change is a Git commit with a timestamp, author, and approval record.

climax.text: GitOps is becoming the cloud-native standard. It unifies deployment, rollback, and compliance in a single workflow.

punchline.text: Git commit to deploy. Git revert to rollback. That simple.

quiz.question: How does GitOps improve infrastructure management?
options: It uses Git as the single source of truth, with automatic sync and built-in audit trails
It eliminates the need for any version control system
It requires all changes to be made directly in the cloud console

details.summary: GitOps uses Git repositories as the single source of truth for infrastructure and application configuration. Changes are made through pull requests, automatically applied by controllers that continuously reconcile the desired state in Git with the actual state of the infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: GitOps brings software development best practices to infrastructure management. Every change is versioned, reviewed, auditable, and reversible, improving reliability and security.
takeaways: Git is the single source of truth for infrastructure state
Changes go through pull requests with reviews and approvals
Controllers automatically reconcile desired and actual state

faq.question: How does GitOps improve over traditional IaC?
faq.answer: Traditional IaC runs imperatively: you execute commands to change infrastructure. GitOps is declarative: you commit the desired state and controllers enforce it continuously. If someone makes a manual change, the controller reverts it to match Git, preventing configuration drift.

faq.question: What tools implement GitOps?
faq.answer: ArgoCD and Flux are the most popular GitOps controllers for Kubernetes. They watch Git repositories and automatically deploy changes to clusters. For broader infrastructure, Terraform with Atlantis or Spacelift provides GitOps workflows for cloud resources beyond Kubernetes.
